newsitem.title: USA: Study finds infant walker injuries still common.
newsitem.headline: Study finds infant walker injuries still common.

text.p: Despite publicity about the hazard, infants continue to be injured while playing in baby walkers, even under supervision, according to a study published on Monday.
Nearly all of the injuries involved falling down a stairs, the report from the Ohio State University College of Medicine in Columbus, Ohio, said.

The findings were based on a review of 271 children treated for walker-related injuries in Ohio from 1993 to 1996. In 78 percent of the cases, the study said, the children were under supervision when the accident occurred.
The study was published in the current issue of Pediatrics, the journal of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

The study said that despite cautions from safety experts and warning labels on the devices themselves, the findings indicate that such injuries remain a problem. It recommended that design standards be imposed so that walkers will not fit through doorways.
